theorems.statement: Finite Newton jets with rational polynomial coefficients and scales in the finite rational prime-valuation group Q_{>0}^x tensor_Z Q are closed under every Newton rescaling whose selected translated root is rational. Candidate scales theta satisfy theta^(r-q)=sigma and are compared exactly by clearing rational valuation denominators. Recursive and one-shot multi-edge substitutions agree exactly.
theorems.occurrence_boundary: The old coarse 2/3-state multiple-root catalogs contained zero natural second-edge rational-multiple-root samples. Targeted common-shift BRC families give 66 verified second-edge samples, including 34 genuinely non-rational radical scales, plus a three-step witness.

theorems.statement: For exact selected algebraic root alpha, coefficients g(alpha) may be represented by rational polynomials g with semantic equality/zero decided by the selected-root gcd/Sturm state. Addition, multiplication, rational scalar multiplication, sign, Taylor coefficients and rational translated-root contact orders are exact without factoring the selector polynomial or constructing a general algebraic field. Therefore algebraic-base Newton recursion remains exact as long as later selected translated roots are rational.
theorems.semantic_zero_law: A nonzero polynomial representative may vanish at alpha. Semantic zero g(alpha)=0 must be filtered before Newton scale ordering.

negative_boundaries.statement: Newton scales with rational prime valuations are exact symbolic multiplicative scales; no floating radical materialization is implied.
Zero second-edge examples in the old coarse catalog is an occurrence census only and is not a theorem that rational-root later edges do not exist.
For algebraic selected alpha, g as a nonzero rational polynomial does not imply g(alpha) is nonzero. Semantic selected-root zero testing precedes scale calculus.
Polynomial representatives modulo a polynomial vanishing at alpha are storage representatives, not a claim of minimal polynomial factorization or a canonical algebraic number field.

The current selected-root evaluation algebra supports the operations required for rational translated-root Newton recursion; it does not promote general inversion, a complete Puiseux engine, or generic algebraic-number arithmetic.

If a translated selected Newton-edge root is itself irrational, the next translation generally introduces another algebraic generator. Exact multi-generator coefficient state remains a separate research frontier.
